newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-MALIK AND AKRAM BOOST PAKISTAN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MALIK AND AKRAM BOOST PAKISTAN.

text.p: Salim Malik and Wasim Akram cracked fine half-centuries to boost Pakistan's total to a respectable 228 for eight in their 46 overs in the first one-day international against New Zealand on Wednesday.
Malik scored a brilliant unbeaten 73 and his captain a breezy 52 after Akram had won the toss and elected to bat before a packed crowd in Gujranwala's Jinnah Stadium.
The pair rescued Pakistan with their sixth-wicket stand of 91 in 15.3 overs after half the side had gone down for 71.
Akram, who missed the two-test series through injury, smashed three sixes and as many fours from 42 balls, taking his personal total in one-day games past 2,000 runs.
Malik finished off the innings with a six off Chris Cairns. His 78-ball knock also included six fours.
Nathan Astle and Chris Harris took two wickets each after Robert Kennedy had made an early breakthrough, removing Zahoor Elahi in his second over.
Opener Saeed Anwar scored 27 from 38 balls while Shahid Afridi lifted Harris for a huge six before falling to a well-judged catch by Dipak Patel at long-on for 16.
The game was reduced to 46 overs from 50 because the sun was shining in the batsmen's eyes at the scheduled start of play.
